sources.citation: Zogbo, Lynell Marchese. 2019. Central vowels in the Kru language family: innovation and areal spreading. In Clem, Jenks & Sande (eds.), Theory and description in African Linguistics (ACAL 47). Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: §2.2.1 'Daloa Bété' covers only the vowel system (three +ATR central vowels, no /ʌ/; cites Zogbo 1981: 15, Zogbo 2005, Kipre 2015 on CVlV syllables); no word for stress or accent in the whole chapter.

sources.citation: Vahoua, Kallet Abréam. 2017. Le ton grammatical du kpɔ̍kʋ̀gbʋ̀, parler kru de Côte d'Ivoire. Cahiers Ivoiriens de Recherche Linguistique 42: 129-147.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Same Gagnoa dialect; grammatical functions of five of the six tonemes; no accent/stress statement (0 hits for 'accent').

sources.citation: Vahoua, Kallet Abréam. 2011. L'instabilité de la voyelle /ʌ/ dans un parler bete (langue kru de Côte d'Ivoire). Nordic Journal of African Studies 20(2): 150-176.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: SIBLING VARIETY: kpɔ̍kʋ̀gbʋ̀ (Kpokolo, canton Paccolo, sous-préfecture de Gagnoa) = Gagnoa Bété, not Daloa. §2.1 lists six tonemes (B, M, H-, H, M-B, B-M); the word 'accent' does not occur.

sources.citation: Kipré Blé, François. 1989. Morphophonologie und Morphotonologie der Nominalphrase einer Kru-Sprache (Bete der Mundart von Daloa). Diss., Universität Bayreuth, 279 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only the DNB table of contents (6 pp.) is online. TOC shows 0.3.1 'Zum phonologischen Wort im Bete' (p.11), ch.1 'Phonologie, Tonologie' pp.14-24 with 1.2 'Die Töne' and 1.3 'Tonale Morpheme' (p.24); no Akzent/Betonung heading anywhere. Body not accessible.

sources.citation: WALS Online, lect 'Bété' (wals_code_bet), mapped to Glottocode dalo1238 / ISO bev; sources Werle & Gbalehi 1976, Koopman 1984
sources.note: 19 values; 13A 'Complex tone system' (from Werle & Gbalehi 1976, i.e. Guiberoua data); no values at all for the stress features 14A-17A.

sources.citation: Werle, Johannes-Martin & Dagou Justin Gbalehi. 1976. Phonologie et morphonologie du bété de la région de Guiberoua. Abidjan: ILA-SIL (Publications conjointes 2), 215 pp. [excerpt pp. 5-7, 82, 85, 150-153, 191-203, 214-215]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes the dakwie dialect of Kosseoa (Guiberoua group A), NOT Daloa (group B). Conclusions p.191: 'Sur le plan du système prosodique notons.. la présence de quatre registres tonals distinctifs; la stabilité du système tonal; l'absence de tons modulés.' No accent/stress statement; TOC (p.214) has no accent section.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative lexicon with many 'bété (Daloa)' forms (§4.6 'Le parler de Daloa se distingue du bété central'); no stress/accent statement.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page and full reference table for dalo1238 (17 references)
sources.note: Beyond the 6 descriptive refs it lists Marchese 1983 Atlas + Listes de lexèmes kru, Zogbo 1980, Monod 1959 (Bété script) and ethnographic items; no phonology article specific to Daloa Bété.

sources.note: The only modern grammar of Daloa Bété (Glottolog 'grammar'; a pedagogical 'Parlons' volume); the series always opens with a phonology chapter covering tones and usually a remark on accent. Google Books has a partial preview (id GXsniVAk4uoC) that could not be opened by automated download.
